name: Holmarc Opto-Mechatronics Limited
sector: Scientific instrumentation, photonics and precision optomechanics
summary: Technical niche and net cash support growth, but recent incremental returns, WIP control limitations, capital deployment and illiquidity constrain attractiveness. A funded base yields 12.04% against a 15% hurdle; cash access and procurement response matter to survival.
identity_note: Annual reports, prospectus and the 19 October eligible SM security-master row agree on identity, 10,050,000 issued shares and the 750-share lot.

quote.kind: official close, not live executable bid

score_note: Canonical exact weights with no overrides. Displays: 5.8 / 6.2 / 4.3. IAS is conditional on the ₹5 lakh reference and explicit funding assumptions.

gates.reason: No substantiated diversion or abuse was established. The financial-statement opinion is unmodified, but WIP control weakness, family influence and disclosed disputes warrant scrutiny, not an accusation.

Signed faces and opening claims reconcile. WIP valuation controls require strengthening, and the gross gratuity roll-forward contains an inconsistent printed line; the net deficit table and balance sheet agree at ₹2.2538 crore. Impairment and tax-claim sensitivities bound rather than erase uncertainty.

A 10% revenue decline, 9% initial margin, 100-day collection and 45-day inventory survive without new capital while paying the full ₹6 crore unit budget and legacy claims. Slower collections or unresponsive inventory can fail. Bank-deposit encumbrance is undisclosed: full-guarantee collateral is an analyst reserve, not a verified lien. Procurement and existing-deposit alternatives are separate from hypothetical rescue.

Actual trades and an eligible SM series establish historical tradability. Large lots relative to turnover, market-making expiry and irregular-trading cautions prevent treating the quote as executable ₹5 lakh capacity.

sections.title: 1. Executive verdict
sections.text:
Holmarc has a genuine technical niche in scientific instruments and optomechanical components, backed by decades of engineering work. It is not yet a demonstrated high-return compounder. FY2026 operating revenue rose 13.6% to ₹42.23 crore, operating EBITDA excluding other income was ₹6.35 crore, and PAT was ₹4.08 crore. CFO of ₹4.63 crore is encouraging, but increased customer advances helped and recent incremental capital returns remain weak. [S1,S2,S4]

At the official ₹128 close on 19 October 2026, equity value is ₹128.64 crore. The funded base case yields 12.04% annualized, below the 15% research hurdle; the bull yields 31.46%, while a funded bear loses 10.47% annually. The upside requires successful commercialization, productivity gains and disciplined reinvestment, not merely a large scientific-equipment market.

BQS is 5.78, GQS 6.15 and IAS 4.345. This is a mixed-quality technical business with an execution-dependent growth opportunity and a weak current setup under the stated hurdle, not a finding of misconduct or inevitable financial distress. Cash-access assumptions, a ₹6 crore industrial-unit purchase, legacy employee obligations and poor trading liquidity matter materially. The ₹5 lakh liquidity reference is illustrative, not a suggested position.

sections.title: 2. Research scope and comparability
sections.text:
Holmarc Opto-Mechatronics Limited; NSE SME HOLMARC; ISIN INE0LXA01019. Research cutoff is 20 October 2026, with the last market observation on 19 October. The company reports standalone accounts with no subsidiary/minority valuation complication. Figures are converted from lakhs into crore. FY2021–23 uses the final prospectus's restated series; FY2024–26 uses audited annual statements and later comparisons. Earlier original revenue labels exclude or reclassify freight, so they are not silently spliced into the restated growth series. [S1,S2,S3,S4]

The FY2023 PBT difference is explained by a ₹0.7384 crore gratuity-provision reversal, not an unexplained cash gap. FY2024 issued shares and weighted EPS shares differ because the IPO occurred during the year. Recent cash-equivalent presentation excludes deposits previously included in an all-cash total; this is a classification change, not missing cash.

No signed H1FY2027 balance sheet or cash flow was available in reviewed sources. Every post-March cash balance is modeled, not reported. The October dividend confirmation and September land-transfer sanction update particular events without supplying a complete current balance sheet. Historical financial-face confidence is High; decision-grade cash availability, inventory valuation and forecast input confidence are Medium. Forward uncertainty remains High.

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and four gates
sections.text:
BQS uses GOV 5, MOAT 6, REV 7, DUR 7, CAP 4, CASH 6, BAL 7 and EXEC 5 at canonical weights, producing 5.78. GQS uses REV 7, DUR 7, EARN 5, CAP 4 and CASH 6, producing 6.15. IAS uses final BQS 5.78, R 4, D 4, P 5 and L 2, producing 4.345. One-decimal half-up displays are 5.8, 6.2 and 4.3. No override or missing-factor reweighting is applied.

G1 Integrity is conditional: no substantiated diversion or abuse was established, but family influence and the auditor's control observation limit assurance. G2 Accounting reliability is conditional: the signed faces and net benefit deficit reconcile, while WIP valuation and a malformed gross-benefit roll-forward require caution. G3 Stress survival is conditional, supported by a source-grounded procurement response without rescue capital; unavailable deposits or weaker working-capital execution can overturn it. G4 Tradability is conditional: actual trades exist, but market-making expiry, sparse turnover and lot granularity impair implementation. [S1,S5,S6,S9,S10,S11]

These judgments do not turn unknown facts into neutral scores. They distinguish bounded uncertainty from a genuinely unfinanceable essential business or an established integrity failure.

sections.title: 4. Business and industry economics
sections.text:
Founded in 1993, Holmarc designs and manufactures scientific and engineering instruments for research, education and industry. Optics, mechanics, electronics and software combine in spectroscopy, microscopy, imaging, thin-film systems, laboratory equipment, positioning stages and optical-table products. Its economic model is skilled, relatively low-volume manufacturing, including customized devices and systems, rather than commodity mass assembly. [S1,S4]

The broad catalogue creates cross-selling and adaptation opportunities, but product counts are not recurring revenue. Buyers need application fit, accuracy, installation and service; institutional purchasing can be price-sensitive and slow. FY2026 goods exports were ₹6.41 crore, approximately 15.2% of operating sales, far below management's long-term 50% export aspiration. Imported materials were ₹2.64 crore, so currency and international logistics affect both sides of the business. [S1]

People are the largest operating input: employee expense was ₹19.43 crore, approximately 46% of sales. Management says manufacturing training can take a year or more. A demand slowdown therefore cannot be modeled as an immediate matching reduction in all costs. Technical differentiation may protect individual projects, but no subscription-like renewal base, broad patent royalty stream or independently quantified market share is established.

sections.title: 5. Moat and competitive position
sections.text:
In-house integration across optics, machining, electronics and software, application-specific engineering and trained staff provide meaningful entry friction. Installation examples and research collaborations support real capability rather than merely a thematic label. The prospectus's FY2023 top-five customer share of 11.86% and top-ten share of 19.09% suggest a diversified historical customer base; these are not verified current concentration figures. [S1,S4]

Competition limits the moat claim. Institutional users may choose cheaper local or imported equipment; management explicitly acknowledges low-cost Chinese competition and affordability-driven academic procurement. Edmund Optics' primary company materials describe custom manufacturing alongside an extensive standard-product marketplace and global engineering/distribution capabilities. This demonstrates credible competing capability, not a valuation comparable or proof that Holmarc cannot win locally. [S1,S14]

MOAT 6 recognizes specialist know-how and customer support while withholding a stronger score without repeat-order economics, independently measured price premiums or persistent excess incremental returns. Brand familiarity, distributor agreements and NDAs are not equivalent to switching costs. The precise profitability and defensibility of each product family remain unsegmented.

sections.title: 6. Revenue growth and decomposition
sections.text:
Comparable operating revenue grew from ₹15.53 crore in FY2021 to ₹21.02 crore in FY2022, ₹29.04 crore in FY2023, ₹33.46 crore in FY2024, ₹37.17 crore in FY2025 and ₹42.23 crore in FY2026. The primary five-year CAGR is 22.15%; three-year CAGR is 13.29%. The five-year window is retained rather than selecting whichever period produces the best score. Its starting REV score is 8, reduced one point for three sustained lower-growth annual outcomes. This is the permitted trajectory adjustment, not an additional small-base penalty. [S1,S2,S3,S4]

FY2026 product data are more informative than a single TAM claim. Breadboards, tabletops, rails and related products generated ₹8.60 crore; laboratory equipment ₹6.08 crore; analytical instruments ₹5.29 crore; physics laboratory equipment ₹5.05 crore. Analytical-instrument sales declined from ₹5.82 crore, while breadboard-related sales grew 28.6%. Product growth is not uniformly strong. The goods-category total of ₹40.97 crore reconciles to operating sales after service and freight/packing revenue. [S1]

Separate physical volume and realized price are not disclosed adequately for a constant-mix demand index. The earlier factory purchases supplied existing Holmarc production and do not establish a large purchased revenue book. The new casting assets may add external component business, but no acquired revenue is fabricated in the historical series or treated as guaranteed organic growth.

sections.title: 7. Growth quality, runway and capital productivity
sections.text:
Management's milestone is ₹100 crore of manufactured revenue with more than 50% in-factory value addition. It plans approximately 400 staff, versus 359 in March, while investing in productivity and distribution. The chairman also acknowledges slower-than-planned growth, replacing regional offices with distributors, limiting experience centres and building online inventory cautiously. These are sensible adaptations, but they are not proof that the original timetable was delivered. [S1]

The June disclosure specifies existing capacity of 7,000 units at 90% utilization and a proposed addition of 100 tonnes. Units and tonnes cannot be added or converted into a precise revenue ramp. The ₹6 crore industrial-unit purchase and September sanction provide infrastructure, not instant fully qualified output. Further construction is needed for the chairman's stated space plan; the model explicitly funds an assumed ₹4 crore beyond the purchase in the base and ₹6 crore in the bull. These construction figures are analytical estimates, not company quotations. [S1,S5,S6]

Recent capital productivity is the main weakness. At a uniform 26% normalized tax rate, three-year incremental operating return on the financing-side capital proxy is about 5.4%, versus an assumed 14–18% capital-cost range. The five-year recovery is much better, approximately 23.2%, so this is not an assertion of permanently destructive economics. The latest full operating-capital measure is ₹22.36 crore, compared with approximately ₹20.36 crore on the simpler equity-plus-debt-minus-cash proxy. CAP 4 reflects weak recent deployment and unproven new cohorts. Reported EPS of ₹4.06 is only slightly above FY2024's ₹3.94; normalized operating EPS remains below FY2023 after IPO dilution and removal of the gratuity reversal and tax credits. EARN 5 distinguishes operating progress from flattering headline comparisons.

sections.title: 8. Governance and consequential disclosures
sections.text:
The two named direct promoter holdings total 62.54%; this is not a separately verified current total promoter-group percentage. Director remuneration fell from ₹2.23 crore to ₹1.46 crore, with changes among executive personnel. Related legal and payroll-service fees were ₹0.03 crore and ₹0.0216 crore. These relationships merit scrutiny, but their existence is not evidence of diversion. The April declaration says no encumbrance was created or invoked during FY2026; it is not a certificate that no pledge existed or remains today. [S1,S8]

The FY2026 financial-statement opinion is unmodified. In the separate internal-control opinion, the auditor states that work-in-progress valuation controls need strengthening. WIP was ₹1.98 crore; this is not a finding of fraud or a quantified misstatement. The annual report describes a broader independent control review and phased implementation, not a completed WIP-specific remediation certificate. [S1]

The notes disclose a disputed ₹17.76 lakh building-tax claim with the municipality's appeal pending before the Kerala High Court, and GST notices under response/adjudication with no quantified adverse exposure. These do not establish final liability or wrongdoing; later outcomes were not verified. The May audit also noted pending title documentation for two HMT assets, while the later chairman's statement says those formalities were completed. Separately, the September Edayar sanction imposes documentation and production conditions. No breach is asserted. Final deeds and commissioning evidence were not reviewed. [S1,S6]

sections.title: 9. Financial forensics and opening claims
sections.text:
Cumulative CFO/PAT is 82.35% over FY2024–26 and 84.99% over FY2022–26. Latest CFO of ₹4.63 crore exceeds PAT, but customer advances increased by ₹1.37 crore, partly offsetting stock and receivable investment. Cash capex of ₹4.09 crore leaves only ₹0.54 crore before financing interest and dividends. This is adequate but mixed cash quality, not a persistent negative-cash override. [S1,S2,S3,S4]

Receivables total ₹8.51 crore, including ₹1.05 crore older than six months and ₹0.61 crore older than one year. The older-than-one-year amount improved from approximately ₹0.74 crore in FY2025, but no doubtful provision is disclosed. Inventory is ₹6.02 crore, including ₹1.98 crore WIP and ₹3.30 crore raw materials. WIP impairment sensitivities of 10% and 25% are analytical tests: stock and equity are reduced, the noncash charge is added back once, and replacement working capital is funded once. No cash release is manufactured from an impairment. [S1]

The ₹38.03 crore opening balance sheet fully reconciles. Ordinary working capital of ₹11.91 crore includes supplier/contractor advances and all statutory, salary, leave, welfare, audit, rent and electricity claims within current liabilities. Current tax of ₹0.2765 crore and bonus of ₹0.2754 crore are separately paid in June 2026. A ₹0.0208 crore tax refund is a single assumed December receipt, also tested with no recovery. Deferred-tax assets and the small tax deposit receive no invented cash credit.

The gratuity obligation is ₹6.09 crore gross, less ₹3.84 crore plan assets, leaving a ₹2.2538 crore net deficit. The plan assets are not free company cash. The model pays the current ₹0.4835 crore over year one and the noncurrent ₹1.7703 crore over the following four years, while funding future employee expense separately. The published gross roll-forward contains inconsistent printed figures; the net table and balance sheet agree. It is not appropriate to substitute the malformed line or deduct the gross obligation again. [S1]

Cash and deposits of ₹11.0918 crore include ₹7.5358 crore term deposits and ₹0.0007 crore earmarked for unclaimed dividends. IPO proceeds were fully utilized by March 2025. The company reports ₹3.0751 crore bank guarantees but does not quantify the deposit lien. The base conservatively reserves that full amount, leaving ₹8.0160 crore opening available cash. This is an assumption, not a disclosed restriction; zero-reserve and all-deposits-unavailable cases are separate. Customer-advance refunds are already working-capital obligations and are not counted again as a duplicate full guarantee loss. [S1,S2]

sections.title: 10. Valuation and dated shareholder model
sections.text:
At ₹128, equity value is ₹128.64 crore and reported FY2026 PE is 31.5×. Using last-reported March cash and debt, EV/operating EBITDA is approximately 18.6–19.1× depending on the guarantee reserve. These are not verified October net-cash multiples: the subsequent asset purchase and other spending reduce available funds. The base's estimated 19 October bridge has ₹1.60 crore available cash, ₹3.33 crore reserved and ₹0.56 crore debt; those figures are model estimates, not company disclosures. [S1,S5,S7,S9,S10]

Monthly accounting runs from March 2026 to 19 October 2031; the investor enters on 19 October 2026. The confirmed ₹0.50 dividend paid on 16 September 2026 reduces the cash bridge but is not a return to that investor. Later dividends are 12% of prior-year modeled profit when a ₹1 crore cash buffer permits. Returns are dated XIRRs, not a terminal-price CAGR that silently omits dividends. Proposed SBI financing is never counted as cash.

Base sales rise to ₹48.56 crore in FY2027, then grow 15%, 15%, 12%, 12% and 10%, reaching an ₹88.61 crore terminal run rate. EBITDA margin moves from 15.5% to 17%, receivables are 75 days and inventory 55 days. The full ₹6 crore unit purchase is paid in year one; construction adds ₹2 crore in each of the next two years, alongside 3% of sales in ongoing capex. At 14× exit EBITDA, operating EV is ₹210.90 crore. Adding ₹11.63 crore available cash, with debt and legacy claims fully settled and ₹6.19 crore reserved cash excluded, gives ₹222.53 crore equity or ₹221.42 per share. Including future dividends yields 12.04% XIRR. The 15% hurdle-entry diagnostic is ₹112.49, not a guaranteed fair value or trade instruction.

Bear sales grow only 3–5%, reaching ₹53.93 crore, with margins recovering from 11.5% to 13%, 95-day receivables and active procurement reducing inventory to 45 days. Optional construction is deferred, but the ₹6 crore unit purchase and essential capex remain funded. A 9× exit gives ₹72.19 per share and −10.47% XIRR. Without the inventory response, the variant has a ₹1.47 crore gap and no return is assigned.

Bull growth of 22%, 25%, 25%, 20%, 18% and 15% produces ₹131.07 crore terminal sales; margins reach 20.5%. Receivables are 65 days, inventory 50 days, construction ₹6 crore beyond the purchase, and ongoing capex 4.5% of sales. An 18× exit gives ₹495.38 per share and 31.46% XIRR. It requires much stronger productivity and commercialization than recent experience. An independent 18× terminal earnings crosscheck gives ₹158.55 for base and ₹286.64 for bull, showing sensitivity to valuation method rather than implying false precision.

sections.title: 11. Funding bridge and credible survival
sections.text:
The base FY2027 cash bridge is opening available cash ₹8.0160 crore plus ₹3.6415 crore operating cash after interest, tax and working capital, less ₹7.4568 crore capex, ₹0.0809 crore debt repayment, ₹0.2765 crore legacy tax, ₹0.2754 crore bonus, ₹0.4835 crore gratuity, ₹0.4613 crore additional guarantee reserve and ₹0.5025 crore pre-entry dividend, plus ₹0.0208 crore tax refund. Closing available cash is ₹2.1414 crore. Monthly cash falls as low as ₹1.43 crore later in the base, so annual totals alone would overstate comfort.

A credible essential-operation stress starts with ₹38 crore revenue, roughly 10% below FY2026, and a 9% margin reflecting a sticky skilled workforce. It allows 100-day receivables, reduces inventory to 45 days and defers optional construction while still paying the ₹6 crore purchase and all modeled legacy claims. It survives without new borrowing or equity with approximately ₹0.49 crore minimum available cash. The inventory response is grounded in management's stated cautious stocking policy and historical inventory levels, not assumed rescue financing. [S1,S5,S6]

Keeping inventory at 50 days makes this conservative-reserve stress marginally unfunded; reverting collections to 120 days also creates a gap. Yet 120-day collection survives if existing deposits are accessible without the assumed guarantee reserve. Conversely, freezing all opening term deposits makes even base expansion unfunded. Because actual collateral terms are undisclosed, these boundaries cannot be presented as an actual default or a proven unavoidable G3 failure. G3 remains Conditional. The no-rescue survivor still ends near ₹53 per share, so operational survival does not establish downside protection at ₹128.

sections.title: 12. Reverse expectations and multibagger feasibility
sections.text:
To earn 15% with base dividends, terminal common equity must reach ₹253.89 crore rather than the modeled ₹222.53 crore. On the same operating path that means approximately 16.1× EBITDA instead of 14×. Alternatively, the constant-growth grid first clears the hurdle at 16% annual revenue growth, reaching ₹102.88 crore, with the same margin, working-capital and reinvestment rules. That is plausible, but it requires sustained improvement over the recent 13.3% trajectory and successful capital deployment.

The base terminal share value is approximately 1.73× the entry price, while the bull is 3.87× before considering dividends. The bull is not a simple extrapolation: its margins, product mix, collection discipline and productivity are stronger, with explicit additional construction and capex. A large addressable market or government research initiative does not fund these assumptions.

P 5 therefore describes a fair but execution-dependent price-implied case rather than an obvious bargain. Growth and margin grids, 9–18× exit multiples, receivable days, WIP write-downs and tax/deposit-access variants expose the dependence. Unfunded paths have no shareholder XIRR. Hypothetical rescue capital is shown separately, including fees, dilution and draw interest, and never used to prove survival.

sections.title: 13. Liquidity and monitoring triggers
sections.text:
A 750-share lot costs ₹96,000 at the observed price. Five lots cost ₹4.8 lakh; a sixth exceeds the ₹5 lakh reference. In the 60-session sample, 56 sessions are observed and four absences are unknown. Conditional zero-filled mean/median traded value is ₹8.19/5.57 lakh, implying 17.95 days at 5% participation, 44.87 days at 2% and 8.97 days at 10%. Observed-only statistics are retained separately. The latest 20 sessions improve to mean/median ₹11.41/9.04 lakh and 11.06 theoretical days at 5%. [S9,S10,S16]

Only seven of the 56 observed sessions, and four of the latest 20, could fit even one current-price lot within 5% turnover. The starting liquidity score of 3 is reduced to 2 for this granularity and unobserved depth. Official cautions effective 21 October indicate fewer than 100 unique PANs, expiry of mandatory market making and irregular SME trading. They are implementation facts, not wrongdoing indicators, and do not apply retroactively to 19 October. [S11,S12,S13]

Upgrade evidence would include positive cash conversion without growing advance dependence, WIP-control remediation, successful commissioning and document completion, productive skilled hiring, and normalized per-share gains on the new capital. Downgrade evidence includes aged collections, inventory losses, unavailable deposits, project overruns or new financing on unattractive terms. Signed H1 accounts and actual payment/collateral evidence matter more than additional NDAs or exhibition attendance. No trading or monitoring automation has been initiated.

sections.title: 14. Classification and decision conditions
sections.text:
Weak setup under the stated price, hurdle and liquidity reference, with a credible technical growth option rather than an established compounder. Business quality is mixed, growth quality is moderate and current investment attractiveness is below the framework's stronger bands. The label concerns capital returns, valuation and implementation; it does not assert misconduct, insolvency or the absence of useful technology.

A lower price, stronger normalized earnings, proven productivity and better incremental returns could improve the assessment independently. Cash and disclosure improvements would strengthen confidence even if the price did not change. A promised loan or assumed rescue would not resolve a stress gate; verified existing liquidity, enforceable financing or a feasible operating response would need to do so.

Scores are not return probabilities. The 15% hurdle is a nominal INR equity convention before personal taxes, not a personalized financial objective. Implementation must be reassessed for the user's actual allocation and live market conditions, neither of which is supplied here.

sections.title: 15. Evidence, assumptions and remaining gaps
sections.text:
Audited annual reports, restated prospectus financials, exchange announcements and official daily market files anchor the report. Source-specific evidence distinguishes verified disclosures, calculations, attributed management statements and analyst assumptions. The full operating model retains taxes, benefit deficits, expenses, advances, dividends, collateral reserves, reinvestment and terminal claims. It does not count gross plan assets, unreceived loan proceeds or the same customer advance twice.

Important uncertainties are actual post-March balances and payment dates, deposit liens, final expansion costs, product-level profitability, payroll productivity, current customer/supplier concentration, WIP accuracy, legal outcomes and live trading depth. The net gratuity deficit is supported despite a malformed gross roll-forward; a quantified GST liability is not invented. A hypothetical ₹1 crore tax shock is a sensitivity, not an estimate of the dispute. Full-guarantee cash reservation is deliberately distinguished from verified restrictions.

The 14–18% capital-cost range, growth, margins, capex, dividend policy, future employee funding and exit multiples are analytical assumptions. Peer capabilities provide context, not automatic multiples. No later legal outcome or completed remediation is implied by absence of a search result. Forecast uncertainty remains High, and new primary evidence can change both funding conclusions and scores.

Deposit collateral requirements are not quantified. Full-guarantee cash reservation is assumed, not a reported lien; alternative availability cases materially change funding.

Exact lender maturities, construction budget, payroll productivity, product margins and current customer/supplier concentration remain uncertain.
The ₹100 crore target, headcount cap and export aspirations are management goals. Capacity units and tonnes cannot form a precise combined output forecast.
Four market sessions are missing observations; live bid/ask depth is unavailable. ₹5 lakh is a reference, not the user’s allocation.
Current pledge balances were not independently verified. The April declaration concerns creation and invocation during FY2026 only.
Forecast uncertainty is High. Multiples, capital costs and scores are analytical conventions, not guaranteed returns or personalized recommendations.
next_steps: Obtain signed H1 cash balances, deposit-lien detail and confirmed industrial-unit payment/commissioning evidence.
Verify remediation of WIP controls, the gratuity roll-forward and current legal outcomes.
Test productivity, product mix, funded construction and current execution depth before upgrading the thesis.

GOV.reason: Main audit opinion is unmodified and disclosed RPT service fees are modest; WIP control weaknesses, family influence and uncertain latest pledge scope limit assurance. No abuse inferred.

MOAT.reason: Integrated optics/mechanics/electronics/software skills and technical customer relationships create entry friction. Global suppliers and low-cost alternatives remain credible; repeat-order economics and durable pricing power are not demonstrated.

REV.reason: Primary five-year comparable CAGR of 22.15% starts at 8. A one-point downward trajectory adjustment reflects three successive lower-growth annual outcomes and a 13.3% three-year CAGR. No additional small-base penalty or forecast upgrade.

DUR.reason: Scientific and industrial instrumentation offers product and export runway, supported by technical capability and new space. Achieving ₹100 crore still requires productivity, qualifications and capital. NDAs are not backlog.

CAP.reason: Recent three-year incremental return is approximately 5.4%, below the assumed 14–18% capital-cost range, despite a stronger five-year recovery. New asset and staffing investments have not earned mature returns.

CASH.reason: Five-year cumulative CFO/PAT is approximately 0.85 and latest CFO exceeds PAT, but three-year conversion is 0.82, customer advances explain part of the improvement and old receivables remain. Net gratuity obligations still need funding.

BAL.reason: Cash and deposits materially exceed ₹0.60 crore debt, with IPO money fully utilized and no assumed new loan. The ₹6 crore purchase, benefit deficit and possible collateral reserve reduce the apparent surplus.

EXEC.reason: Technical products, installations and sanctioned expansion demonstrate work done. Management acknowledges slow commercial growth and changed IPO-era marketing plans; commissioning, productivity and cash returns remain unfinished tests.

EARN.reason: Recurring operating earnings are positive, but the FY2023 gratuity reversal, current tax credits and IPO dilution distort headline growth. Normalized per-share operating earnings remain below FY2023 despite higher revenue.

R.reason: Funded base XIRR of 12.0415% minus the 15% hurdle is −2.9585 percentage points, within the canonical −4 to −2 band.

D.reason: The funded bear price of ₹72.19 versus ₹128 implies material loss; stronger stress or unavailable deposits can cause funding gaps. A credible inventory response survives without rescue, but buffers are not wide.

P.reason: The 15% hurdle needs about 16.1× terminal EBITDA on the base path or 16% constant growth with a 14× exit. This is plausible but execution-dependent, not a conservative margin of safety.

L.reason: The conditional 60-day exit estimate of 17.95 days starts at 3. A ₹96,000 lot fits 5% participation on only seven of 56 observed days; mandatory market making has ended. Lot granularity and unknown depth warrant 2.

claim_mapping.item: Available cash after assumed full-guarantee reserve
claim_mapping.detail: Available cash is ₹8.0160 crore. The ₹3.0751 crore reserve is conservative, not a disclosed lien. Zero-reserve and all-term-deposits-unavailable alternatives are explicit.
Held outside operating cash and scaled with future business; terminal reserve is excluded. Performance and advance guarantees are contingent, not automatically payable.
Paid June2027 in main scenarios as a prudential assumption, not a finding that the dispute has been lost.
No liability estimate is fabricated. A separate ₹1 crore hypothetical cash shock tests vulnerability, not probability or legal merits.

Rounded note components are ₹0.8322 crore performance and ₹2.24 crore advances, totaling ₹3.0722 crore. The face total is ₹3.0751 crore; the reserve uses that larger amount. Customer-advance refunds already enter working capital and are not duplicated as a full guarantee loss.

Full disclosed budget paid ₹3 crore in June and ₹3 crore in September 2026 in the model. Exact cash dates are unverified; an all-June variant is supplied. The proposed SBI loan is not assumed received.
Paid 16 September 2026 according to the issuer. It reduces cash but is not a return for the 19 October investor.
Base assumes ₹2 crore in FY2028 and FY2029 for new space, not an issuer quotation. Bull assumes ₹6 crore; bear and survival defer this discretionary building.
No material separate acquisitionprice, capitalcreditor or noncancellableleaseclaim identified atMarch31. Known₹6crore laterassetpurchase is modeled in full; no purchaseofsubsidiaryorNCIassumed.

limitations: Close/last is historical, not executable bid. No bid-ask spread or depth. Absent sessions must not be interpreted as no trade unless listed throughout and not missing data. Recent IPO prelisting dates are not zero trading days; use shortened sample. Series changes/multiple rows/corporate actions require issuer review. Raw turnover in INR; exit assumes constant turnover and participation, no circuits or impact.
